findings.title: macOS available-memory estimate counts speculative pages twice
findings.reproduction: Run python3 docs/audits/AUD-004-harnesses/macos-memory.py. It extracts and compiles the unchanged page-summing expression from ffi.rs. The synthetic statistics contain 262144 free pages (including 131072 speculative), 131072 inactive pages, zero purgeable pages and a 4096-byte page size. No Argon2 or large allocation runs.
findings.expected: Speculative pages must not be added to free_count a second time: Apple XNU explicitly includes them in free_count. This fixture represents 1610612736 bytes in the free-plus-inactive estimate.
findings.observed: The production arithmetic reports 2147483648 bytes, allowing the 2 GiB default threshold although the non-duplicated estimate is 1.5 GiB. The assertion fails with left 2147483648, right 1610612736.
findings.impact: On macOS the preliminary resource check can overstate available RAM and admit an operation it should refuse. This raises the risk of memory pressure, swapping or interruption. A native macOS OOM event was not induced; the arithmetic defect, not an actual crash, is demonstrated. Encryption formulas and existing containers are unaffected.
findings.recommendedFix: Remove duplicate accounting of speculative pages and review overlap of the remaining counters against the Apple API contract. Keep the estimator conservative and document that availability is advisory. Consider releasing the Mach host send right and adding a resource margin separately.
findings.requiredVerification: Add a pure estimator regression using overlapping counters, boundary tests around 2 GiB and non-zero levels, and a macOS integration check. Confirm refusal without allocation when the non-duplicated estimate is below the requested memory.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not a demonstrated cryptographic failure or global recovery failure; fix before the next macOS distribution.

findings.title: Both launchers reject genuine binary-mode sha256sum records
findings.reproduction: Run python3 docs/audits/AUD-004-harnesses/checksum-format.py. It creates a public HTML fixture and uses the real sha256sum --text and --binary commands, then calls the Python loader and starts the native launcher with a bounded timeout.
findings.expected: A supported binary-mode checksum line has 64 hexadecimal digits, one space, an asterisk and the filename. Both implementations explicitly attempt to support the binary marker; their tests should use actual tool output.
findings.observed: Text-mode records are accepted by both launchers. Binary-mode records are rejected by both because split_once/partition requires two spaces. The existing native test writes two spaces before the asterisk, which is not sha256sum --binary output.
findings.impact: A valid HTML file cannot start when its sidecar was produced in binary mode. The integrity check fails closed; this does not allow substituted content or expose secrets. The shipped text-mode sidecars continue to work.
findings.recommendedFix: Parse the fixed hash field followed by a space and the text/binary marker; retain single-filename, extension and path checks. Do not strip arbitrary leading asterisks from the filename.
findings.requiredVerification: Use literal output from sha256sum --text and --binary in both launcher suites; keep tamper, traversal, duplicate-line and wrong-filename refusals.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded compatibility issue with a working text-mode alternative.

findings.title: Release archives omit notices for linked Rust dependencies
findings.reproduction: Build the native and browser artifacts, package linux-x86_64, linux-x86_64-ssse3 and browser into the local evidence packages directory, then run python3 docs/audits/AUD-004-harnesses/licenses.py.
findings.expected: The distribution should carry the applicable license and attribution notices of code it includes. A concrete case is bech32 0.12.0, declared MIT in the locked package metadata and used by src/wallet.rs; its LICENSE-MIT identifies Copyright (c) 2017 Clark Moody and requires retaining the notices.
findings.observed: All three freshly generated archives include the project license, Argon2 license and EFF notice but lack the bech32 copyright notice. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md covers Argon2 and EFF and refers to Cargo.lock for Rust crates, without shipping those license texts or a complete Rust attribution bundle.
findings.impact: Distribution metadata is incomplete. This is a packaging defect, not a mnemonic leak or cryptographic weakness. The concrete reproduced omission is bech32; this is not an exhaustive legal assessment of every dependency license.
findings.recommendedFix: Generate a deterministic third-party license/notice bundle from the locked dependencies actually included in native and WASM artifacts, review it, and add it to every relevant archive.
findings.requiredVerification: Inspect unpacked native and browser packages for the full bech32 notice and all other required selected-license notices; add a packaging gate and confirm reproducible ordering.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not a cryptographic acceptance blocker; complete the notices before redistributing updated artifacts.

remediation.evidence: src/engine/ffi.rs: the macOS estimate is now free_count + inactive_count, computed by the pure function mach_available_bytes, which every OS compiles in tests; the unsafe Mach query stays in ffi.rs. Speculative pages are not added again, because Apple's vm_statistics.h (revision cited above) counts them in free_count. purgeable_count is no longer added either: purgeable pages stay on the active and inactive queues, so the sum could repeat inactive pages; a smaller estimate only refuses earlier. The doc comment that described the old four-counter sum is corrected; no other document stated the formula. Unit test engine::ffi::tests::mach_estimate_does_not_count_speculative_pages_twice: the reproduced counters (262144 free including 131072 speculative, 131072 inactive, 4096-byte pages) give 1610612736 bytes, below the 2147483648 bytes of the default level; exact-boundary and one-page-short values at memory levels 0 and 1; 16 KiB pages and u32::MAX counters without overflow. cargo test --locked --lib engine:: passed 15, one full-size test ignored; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings passed; cargo clippy --locked --offline --target aarch64-apple-darwin --all-targets -- -D warnings passed with a stand-in C compiler (type check only; nothing linked or run). Missing: a native macOS run. The macOS CI job runs engine::native::tests::refuses_more_memory_than_the_computer_reports, which asks for more than the real estimate and expects a refusal before any allocation.

src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs and packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py each gain split_checksum_line: the 64-character digest, one space, then exactly one marker, a second space (text mode) or * (binary mode), then the name. A further * stays part of the name and fails the name match, so arbitrary leading asterisks are no longer stripped. The one-line, .html, plain-name and hexadecimal-digest rules are unchanged; upper-case digits stay accepted, as before. New tests serve::tests::accepts_the_text_and_binary_output_of_sha256sum and test_accepts_the_text_and_binary_output_of_sha256sum in scripts/verify-fast-mode-script.py use the literal GNU sha256sum --text and --binary lines for the test page. The refusal lists add <hex>*name, a tab separator, a second line in binary mode, *../tool.html and a non-hexadecimal digit; tamper, traversal, duplicate-line and wrong-name refusals are kept. The former test line <hex>  *tool.html, which sha256sum never writes, is now refused as naming *tool.html. The refusal message and web/README.md name both forms. cargo test --locked --bin mhfe passed 36; python3 scripts/verify-fast-mode-script.py passed 14; after cargo build --locked --release, the unchanged harness checksum-format.py accepts both modes in both launchers (remediation-checksum-format.log).

First step (2547a26): the bech32 0.12.0 LICENSE-MIT text was added to THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md; the check of the shipped crates then showed that 79 more crates lacked their notices. Second step (5eed93c): new scripts/third-party-licenses.py (Python standard library) takes the union of cargo tree --locked --offline -e normal,no-proc-macro over x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, x86_64-apple-darwin and aarch64-apple-darwin, each with and without ssse3, and wasm32-unknown-unknown with wasm; reads each crate's licence expression and files through cargo metadata --locked --offline --all-features from the local registry; and writes THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md: 84 crates, 50 distinct texts, each crate with its version, expression, licence used and a link to its text. Choice rule: every part joined by AND is required (Unicode-3.0 next to MIT for unicode-ident); among alternatives joined by OR, MIT when offered, otherwise Apache-2.0, otherwise the only licence; anything else stops the script. Texts are the crates' own files, copied unchanged with their copyright lines (LF line endings, trailing blank space dropped), and byte-identical texts are grouped. block2, objc2, objc2-encode and dispatch2 publish no licence file: their entries say so and carry the SPDX MIT text with the holders from authors (Mads Marquart; for dispatch2 Mads Marquart, Mary). bitcoin_hashes (CC0-1.0) publishes none either and gets the CC0 1.0 legal code that bip39 and hex-conservative ship. No crate was left unresolved. --check regenerates in memory and fails on any difference; scripts/check.sh, which CI runs, now runs cargo fetch --locked and then this check. scripts/package-release.sh copies THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md next to THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md into every archive, and then runs the new scripts/check-release-artifacts.sh --archives, which requires LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md, byte for byte as in the checkout, in every tar.gz and zip archive. The canonical container build packs through the same script. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md now holds only material that is not a crate and points to the new file; the bech32 section moved into it. It adds the browser package's JavaScript: the Emscripten 6.0.10 LICENSE (MIT or University of Illinois/NCSA) and musl COPYRIGHT, taken from the local pinned Emscripten installation, and the wasm-bindgen 0.2.128 MIT notice from wasm-bindgen-cli-support. README names both files. Results: generator wrote the file and --check passed; after a line was appended, --check failed with exit 1, and it passed again after the file was restored (remediation2-generator.log); scripts/package-release.sh v0.4.0 <scratch> linux-x86_64 browser passed its new archive check, and both archives hold the three files identical to the checkout (remediation2-packaging.log, remediation2-archive-contents.log); a tar.gz without the file and one with a changed copy were refused, and a zip with all three was accepted (remediation2-archive-check.log); bash -n passed on the three edited shell scripts; cargo fmt --check passed. Not run: the canonical container build and the Windows and macOS archives, which use the same packaging script.

No independent cryptographic proof, side-channel measurement, adversarial hardware fault campaign or exhaustive audit of transitive library internals. C integration and relevant allocation/thread/wipe paths were reviewed.
Host/browser compromise, swap, core dumps and immutable/dependency buffers remain outside guaranteed erasure. No real wallet material was used.

recommendations: Promote the bounded real-browser probe into CI: exercise actual workers, both isolation modes, cancellation during execution and immediate restart. Node tests with stand-in workers do not replace this coverage.

After fixing macOS accounting, consider a conservative memory margin and Linux cgroup-aware limits. /proc/meminfo alone does not establish process/container headroom; successful lazy allocation does not guarantee later pages can be committed.

Document what happens if application-supplied onProgress/onUnverified callbacks throw, and preferably reject/cancel the client operation explicitly. The raw WASM callback path handles exceptions as cancellation, while page-side event callbacks currently propagate them to the browser event loop.

The EFF membership/count warning is only a heuristic. Four repeated or deliberately chosen dictionary words should not look equivalent to four independent dice draws; consider an always-visible random-selection reminder and a repetition warning without claiming to measure password entropy.
